title: Move DB/temp-dir cleanup into addTearDown across epic_21_multi_account_test.dart so failed assertions don't leak resources
rule: TQ-6 / Nygard lens (cleanup on the failure path)
why: 20 of this file's ~30 tests acquire a DeviceRegistryDatabase/UserDatabase/temp Directory and release it as the very last statement of the test body instead of via addTearDown/tearDown -- the correct pattern the SAME file already uses in Stories 21.1, 21.3, and 21.4 (`tearDown(() => registry.close())` at lines 32/208/257). When an earlier expect() in one of the 20 ad-hoc tests fails, execution stops before the cleanup line runs: the temp directory and its .db file are never deleted, and the Drift database handle is never closed. On a local edit-test-rerun loop this leaks a fresh systemTemp directory on every failed run; a leaked open DB handle mid-suite risks 'database is locked'-style failures bleeding into unrelated tests later in the same run, muddying CI triage of an unrelated failure.
recommendation: Replace every trailing `await registry.close()` / `await db.close()` / `await tempDir.delete(recursive: true)` with `addTearDown(() => ...)` registered immediately after the resource is created, mirroring the tearDown(() => registry.close()) pattern already used in this file's Stories 21.1/21.3/21.4 groups.
acceptance_criteria: No test body in this file calls .close()/.delete(recursive on a resource it created without a preceding addTearDown for that same resource
A deliberately-failing expect() inserted before the old cleanup line still results in the temp dir/DB being cleaned up (verified via addTearDown running)

corrections: The 'database is locked-style failures bleeding into unrelated tests' mechanism is overstated: all DBs cited use NativeDatabase.memory() and each tempDir has a unique generated name, so cross-test file-lock contention is implausible. The real, supportable cost is leaked temp directories under Directory.systemTemp accumulating across local failed test runs, which is still a legitimate P2.
